items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: I played with Kelly before the pressure. Then after the pressure.

ctx.x: Long after Buddy. Yeah. Long after. Did you play with Kelly before the pressure or after?

I played with Kelly before the pressure. Then after the pressure. There was lots of times that I carried my own band. That's how many men are scared of me today. They don't want to be bothering me. They scared me to take their way.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1960-07-29
items.q: And when he started with us in Kelly's band, he was a drummer.

ctx.x: I just wonder, was it before World War I or... Um... Oh yeah, that's before World War I. It was coming. What was his right name?

Who is it? You don't know? I just don't know. And Tano says that you asked me about none of the musicians' right name. To tell the truth about it. That's the point you said. Well you're the only one who knows Ambrose's name, man. I never got that. Well some only know a name. All right, you take, for instance, you take Howard. I just got Howard's name. This was about two years ago, as long as I've been knowing him. And when he started with us in Kelly's band, he was a drummer. And I just know him lately here.…
No way. Never goes into that. Well let me ask you something. When you wanted to get in touch with these fellas for jobs, how did you find them if you didn't know their right names?

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-02-07
items.q: No, it was like he would lead all, lead the joint, and I believe right on the end, not above him, on the end. That would send him right through it all the time.

ctx.x: Sitting there for, I played along with Sim Gisby and everybody. Yeah. I never played along with them.
Getting back a bit to Chris Kelly, did Chris ever play with a mute?
Mute? Yeah, did he use mute? Oh, he, Chris had, Chris had, uh, mute the Vulcan.
